comp_0.description:
What it does The control policy of the Iterator template. It decides whether a failed item ends the loop.

How it works The Iterator consults it after every failed item, passing the counts so far and its own settings. It answers exit when Continue On Error is off or the failures have reached Max Failures, and continue otherwise; on exit the Iterator fails the run. If it cannot be reached, the Iterator fails the run rather than carrying on unchecked.

Configure
- Nothing here; set Continue On Error and Max Failures on the Iterator FSM.

In and out In: completed, failed, total, last_error, continue_on_error and max_failures. Out: should_exit and exit_reason.

Use it when
- You need different stopping rules for a loop: change this policy, and the Iterator follows it.
comp_0.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: policy
name: Iterator Policy
description: >
  Internal control policy for the Iterator. Consulted after each failed item,
  it ends the loop, failing the run, when Continue On Error is off or Max
  Failures is reached.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    request_data:
      completed: integer (optional) - Items finished so far.
      failed: integer (optional) - Items failed so far.
      total: integer (optional) - Items in the array.
      last_error: string (optional) - The error of the item that just failed.
      continue_on_error: boolean (optional) - The Iterator's Continue On Error setting.
      max_failures: integer (optional) - The Iterator's Max Failures setting; 0 means no limit.
    response_data:
      should_exit: boolean - True when the loop must stop.
      exit_reason: string - Why the loop stops; empty when it continues.

policy_states:
  - continue
  - exit

comp_2.description:
What it does The engine of the Iterator template. It runs the handler slot once for every item of the incoming list and gathers the results in list order.

How it works It reads the list at Item Key, then invokes the handler with each item as iterator_item, its position as iterator_index and the list length as iterator_total, alongside the original data. Max Parallel bounds how many run at once. After a failed item it asks the paired policy whether to carry on. When the policy stops the loop, or cannot be reached, items not yet started are skipped, the ones already running are awaited, and the run fails with the failed item's error.

Configure
- Item Key - where the list is, as a dotted path.
- Max Parallel - items run at once, 1 to 50.
- Continue On Error and Max Failures - whether a failure fails the run (by default it does).

In and out In: the data holding the list. Out: results, total, completed, failed and errors, as data and as a JSON artifact.

Use it when
- You are editing how the Iterator template loops; wire work into the handler slot instead of changing this script.
comp_2.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: fsm
name: Iterator
description: >
  FSM layer that runs its handler slot once per item of an incoming array,
  in order or a bounded number at a time, and returns every item's result
  in input order. After a failed item the paired policy decides whether to
  carry on; when it stops the loop, the run fails.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    artifact_type_input: optional(json)
    artifact_type_output: json
    request_data:
      items: array (optional) - The array to iterate; read from Item Key, which may be a dotted path.
    response_data:
      results: array - Each item's response_data in input order; null for a failed item.
      total: integer - How many items there were.
      completed: integer - How many items the handler finished.
      failed: integer - How many items failed; above 0 only when Continue On Error is on.
      errors: array - index and error for each failed item, in input order.

state_ports:
  - port_name: handler
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none

policy_ports:
  - port_name: policy
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    response_data:
      should_exit: boolean - True when the loop must stop.
      exit_reason: string (optional) - Why the loop stops.

input_parameters:
  - name: item_key
    type: text
    label: Item Key
    default: items
    description: Where the array is in the incoming data; a dotted path such as state_1.files works.
  - name: max_parallel
    type: integer
    label: Max Parallel
    default: 1
    description: How many items run at once; 1 runs them strictly in order.
  - name: continue_on_error
    type: boolean
    label: Continue On Error
    default: false
    description: Off (default) fails the run at the first failed item. On records failures in errors and carries on.
  - name: max_failures
    type: integer
    label: Max Failures
    default: 0
    description: With Continue On Error on, fail the run once this many items have failed; 0 means no limit.

comp_3.description:
What it does The exit of the Iterator template. It returns the collected results of every item.

How it works Takes the collected results and returns them as the result of the nested run, so the parent flow can carry on. It adds nothing of its own.

Configure Nothing.

In and out In: the collected results of every item. Out: the same data, as the template's result.

Use it when It comes with the Iterator template. You do not add it separately.

orchestration.description:
What it does Runs one step for every item of a list - each file, each row, each customer - and collects the results, instead of you wiring the same step again and again.

How it works Wire the component that handles one item into the handler slot. The template reads the list from the incoming data, then runs the handler once per item, passing the item along with its position and the original data. Items run one after another by default, or a few at a time when you raise Max Parallel. Every item's result comes back in the order of the list. By default the first failed item fails the run with that item's error, so a batch never reports success over a broken item. Turn on Continue On Error to carry on past failures instead: each one is listed with its error, and Max Failures still fails the run once too many have failed. The paired policy makes that decision, from your settings.

Configure (on the FSM component inside)
- Item Key - where the list is in the incoming data, for example items or state_1.files.
- Max Parallel - how many items run at once; 1 keeps them strictly in order.
- Continue On Error - off (default) fails the run at the first failed item; on carries on and lists the failures.
- Max Failures - with Continue On Error on, fail the run once this many items have failed; 0 means no limit.

In and out In: data holding the list at Item Key. Out: results (one per item, in order), total, completed, failed and errors.

Use it when
- The same step must run over every file, record or message in a list.
- You want a batch to carry on past a bad item and report which ones failed.
- A list is long enough that running a few items at a time saves real time.
orchestration.name: ITERATOR (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
